title: Using Claude Responsibly: Limits, Privacy, and Values

options.text: A fluent, confident statement that is false or unsupported
Any answer longer than a paragraph

questions.explanation: Hallucinations are statements that are factually wrong or inconsistent with the provided material, often delivered confidently.

questions.prompt: Which techniques reduce hallucinations? Select all that apply.

options.text: Allowing Claude to say "I don't know"
Telling Claude to sound more confident

questions.explanation: Permission to admit uncertainty, grounding in quotes and citations, and restricting to provided material all help. Confidence isn't accuracy.

questions.prompt: A chat that isn't saved to history, memory, or chat search is called an ____ chat.
questions.explanation: Incognito chats (the ghost icon) aren't saved to chat history, memory, or search.

questions.prompt: Order the core values in Claude's constitution by priority.
questions.explanation: The constitution orders the properties as broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant with Anthropic's guidelines, and genuinely helpful, applied holistically.

questions.prompt: Match each account type to its default data policy (as of writing).

pairs.right: Not used for training by default

questions.explanation: Consumer users choose whether their data trains models (5-year vs 30-day retention); commercial accounts aren't used for training by default.

questions.prompt: You delete a conversation. What happens to memory entries generated from it?

options.text: They aren't automatically removed; delete them in Settings > Memory

questions.explanation: The Help Center notes that when a conversation expires or is deleted, related memory entries generated from it won't be removed, so clean them up in Settings > Memory.
